meta.title: Finnish B2 Upper Intermediate
meta.subtitle: 1500 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Finnish → English (see the Finnish, recall the meaning) and English → Finnish (see an English meaning, recall the Finnish). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 1500 words of Finnish for an upper-intermediate learner, aligned to B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand the main ideas of complex text on both concrete and abstract topics, including technical discussions in their field of specialisation' — a learner here is able to interact with a degree of fluency and spontaneity that makes regular interaction with native speakers quite possible without strain for either party, and to produce clear, detailed text on a wide range of subjects and explain a viewpoint on a topical issue, giving the advantages and disadvantages of various options. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: Finnish has an examination graded to these levels (the National Certificates of Language Proficiency, YKI), but no graded word list for it was found published, so this deck is not an examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 278 of the 1500 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — politics and public administration, the law and the courts, the economy and finance, science and research, technology, the environment and natural resources, health and the mind, the arts, literature and the media, history and society, argument and evaluation — the words for claims, evidence, causes and consequences — the formal connectors of written Finnish, words for describing, and the verbs of reporting, analysing and persuading — and the other 1222 are the commonest remaining words of everyday Finnish, taken from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles and counted by the WHOLE word, every case of a noun and every form of a verb added together. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Verbs are given as Finnish dictionaries give them, in the first infinitive (syödä "to eat", puhua "to speak"). The 814 nouns show their plural, their genitive, their partitive and their plural partitive, the forms consonant gradation and stem changes make hard to guess (käsi, kädet, käden, kättä, käsiä), and behind the All forms fold every case in both numbers; the 277 verbs show their "I" and "he, she" forms, their past and their perfect (syödä: syön, syö, söi, on syönyt), and behind the fold the present, the negative, the past, the perfect, the conditional and the imperative by person, and the passive. The Finnish Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the letters and their sounds. Real example sentences come with 1394 of the 1500 words, three apiece for 1210 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings and forms: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
